Discover our English Courses How to apply Student services How to reach us in Rome Contact Us Welcome to Link Campus University Link Campus University (LCU) is a private university in Rome, founded in 1999 as a subsidiary of the University of Malta in Italy. Twelve years later, LCU established itself as an independent institution of higher education, governed by the Italian regulatory system for universities. It was recognized as such by the Italian regulation decree: Ministry of Education, University, and Research Decree No. 374, 21st September 2011. LCU was founded with a mission: to create an international imprint by linking students from different nations and cultures in a shared university experience . Till today, it has remained true to its history and its international calling. The university combines the English system’s educational strategies with Italian culture and teaching methods . Some courses are taught in Italian, but most of the degree courses, at both the bachelor's and master's levels, are taught in English. LCU offers a wide range of prestigious Master's programs. Each combines scientific rigor with an interdisciplinary and multicultural approach, one of the university’s major strengths. Link Campus University is situated in a magnificent historical complex . The main building - the Manor of San Pio V - is immersed in a wonderful park located not far from the center of Rome , right next door to the Vatican City . The manor building was commissioned by the newly elected Pope V , Antonio Ghislieri. Upon completion of the building in 1567 , he made it his summer residence. Over the years, the building changed hands several times, becoming the property of an old bankers’ family from Siena, the Chigi family , in 1655 . Around this time, the House of Chigi acquired several Italian estates, the most important of which was Palazzo Chigi in central Rome. In 1916, Palazzo Chigi was purchased by the Kingdom of Italy. It currently serves as the seat of the Italian government. The Manor of San Pio V and surrounding gardens stayed in the hands of the House of Chigi's descendants until 2016, when the property was acquired by Link Campus University . Thus, not only does Link Campus University offer the opportunity to study in a highly innovative educational environment , it also offers a campus atmosphere steeped in history and beauty. Discover our English Courses How to apply Student services How to reach us in Rome Contact Us Welcome to Link Campus University Link Campus University (LCU) is a private university in Rome, founded in 1999 as a subsidiary of the University of Malta in Italy. Twelve years later, LCU established itself as an independent institution of higher education, governed by the Italian regulatory system for universities. It was recognized as such by the Italian regulation decree: Ministry of Education, University, and Research Decree No. 374, 21st September 2011. LCU was founded with a mission: to create an international imprint by linking students from different nations and cultures in a shared university experience . Till today, it has remained true to its history and its international calling. The university combines the English system’s educational strategies with Italian culture and teaching methods . Some courses are taught in Italian, but most of the degree courses, at both the bachelor's and master's levels, are taught in English. LCU offers a wide range of prestigious Master's programs. Each combines scientific rigor with an interdisciplinary and multicultural approach, one of the university’s major strengths. Link Campus University is situated in a magnificent historical complex . The main building - the Manor of San Pio V - is immersed in a wonderful park located not far from the center of Rome , right next door to the Vatican City . The manor building was commissioned by the newly elected Pope V , Antonio Ghislieri. Upon completion of the building in 1567 , he made it his summer residence. Over the years, the building changed hands several times, becoming the property of an old bankers’ family from Siena, the Chigi family , in 1655 . Around this time, the House of Chigi acquired several Italian estates, the most important of which was Palazzo Chigi in central Rome. In 1916, Palazzo Chigi was purchased by the Kingdom of Italy. It currently serves as the seat of the Italian government. The Manor of San Pio V and surrounding gardens stayed in the hands of the House of Chigi's descendants until 2016, when the property was acquired by Link Campus University . Thus, not only does Link Campus University offer the opportunity to study in a highly innovative educational environment , it also offers a campus atmosphere steeped in history and beauty. Discover our English Courses How to apply Student services How to reach us in Rome Contact Us How to reach us in Rome By Metro: Line A direction towards Battistini. Get off at the Cornelia stop. Walk for 10 minutes toward Villa Carpegna, reaching Via Gregorio VII, 601; alternatively, take bus 916 (Piazza Venezia) or 791 (Nervi / Palazzo Sport) for two stops to Villa Carpegna. By Bus: Piazza della Repubblica (Termini train station) Take bus 64 and get off at Cavalleggeri / San Pietro, then hop on bus 881, 916, or 98 and get off at Gregorio VII / Villa Carpegna. From Piazza Venezia: Take bus 916 (Andersen) and get off at Gregorio VII / Villa Carpegna. From Palazzetto dello Sport - Nervi stop: take bus 791 (Cornelia) and get off at Gregorio VII / Villa Carpegna. By car: Those coming from the south (Naples), after entering the Grande Raccordo Anulare, can take: • Exit 1 for SS1 towards Roma Centro-Aurelio / Aurelia / Porto Civitavecchia. • Follow the signs for Roma Centro / Aurelio, / Città del Vaticano. Continue on Via Aurelia / State Road 1, from La Spezia / SS1. • Take Via Aurelia Antica toward Via Gregorio VII. Those coming from the north (Florence) can take: • A1 / E35 in the direction of Strada Statale 1 Variante Aurelia of La Spezia in Rome. • Take exit 1 from the A90. Continue on State Road 1 Variante Aurelia of La Spezia. • Take Via Aurelia Antica toward Via Gregorio VII in Rome. By plane: From Ciampino Airport: • Take bus shuttle to Termini or take bus 520 (Cinecittà - MA) • Get off at the Tuscolana / Cinecittà stop • Take Metro A (Battistini) • Get off at Cornelia stop. Walk 10 minutes toward Villa Carpegna, reaching Via Gregorio VII, 601, alternatively, take bus 916 (Piazza Venezia) or 791 (Nervi / Palazzo Sport) for two stops to Villa Carpegna. From Fiumicino Airport: • Take the train to Termini station or take a taxi; • Take Metro Line A (Battistini); • Get off at the Cornelia stop. Walk for 10 minutes toward Villa Carpegna, reaching Via Gregorio VII, 601; alternatively, take bus 916 (Piazza Venezia) or 791 (Nervi / Palazzo Sport) for two stops to Villa Carpegna. Discover our English Courses How to apply Student services How to reach us in Rome Contact Us Welcome to Link Campus University Link Campus University (LCU) is a private university in Rome, founded in 1999 as a subsidiary of the University of Malta in Italy. Twelve years later, LCU established itself as an independent institution of higher education, governed by the Italian regulatory system for universities. It was recognized as such by the Italian regulation decree: Ministry of Education, University, and Research Decree No. 374, 21st September 2011. LCU was founded with a mission: to create an international imprint by linking students from different nations and cultures in a shared university experience . Till today, it has remained true to its history and its international calling. The university combines the English system’s educational strategies with Italian culture and teaching methods . Some courses are taught in Italian, but most of the degree courses, at both the bachelor's and master's levels, are taught in English. LCU offers a wide range of prestigious Master's programs. Each combines scientific rigor with an interdisciplinary and multicultural approach, one of the university’s major strengths. Link Campus University is situated in a magnificent historical complex . The main building - the Manor of San Pio V - is immersed in a wonderful park located not far from the center of Rome , right next door to the Vatican City . The manor building was commissioned by the newly elected Pope V , Antonio Ghislieri. Upon completion of the building in 1567 , he made it his summer residence. Over the years, the building changed hands several times, becoming the property of an old bankers’ family from Siena, the Chigi family , in 1655 . Around this time, the House of Chigi acquired several Italian estates, the most important of which was Palazzo Chigi in central Rome. In 1916, Palazzo Chigi was purchased by the Kingdom of Italy. It currently serves as the seat of the Italian government. The Manor of San Pio V and surrounding gardens stayed in the hands of the House of Chigi's descendants until 2016, when the property was acquired by Link Campus University . Thus, not only does Link Campus University offer the opportunity to study in a highly innovative educational environment , it also offers a campus atmosphere steeped in history and beauty. Discover our English Courses How to apply Student services How to reach us in Rome Contact Us Welcome to Link Campus University Link Campus University (LCU) is a private university in Rome, founded in 1999 as a subsidiary of the University of Malta in Italy. Twelve years later, LCU established itself as an independent institution of higher education, governed by the Italian regulatory system for universities. It was recognized as such by the Italian regulation decree: Ministry of Education, University, and Research Decree No. 374, 21st September 2011. LCU was founded with a mission: to create an international imprint by linking students from different nations and cultures in a shared university experience . Till today, it has remained true to its history and its international calling. The university combines the English system’s educational strategies with Italian culture and teaching methods . Some courses are taught in Italian, but most of the degree courses, at both the bachelor's and master's levels, are taught in English. LCU offers a wide range of prestigious Master's programs. Each combines scientific rigor with an interdisciplinary and multicultural approach, one of the university’s major strengths. Link Campus University is situated in a magnificent historical complex . The main building - the Manor of San Pio V - is immersed in a wonderful park located not far from the center of Rome , right next door to the Vatican City . The manor building was commissioned by the newly elected Pope V , Antonio Ghislieri. Upon completion of the building in 1567 , he made it his summer residence. Over the years, the building changed hands several times, becoming the property of an old bankers’ family from Siena, the Chigi family , in 1655 . Around this time, the House of Chigi acquired several Italian estates, the most important of which was Palazzo Chigi in central Rome. In 1916, Palazzo Chigi was purchased by the Kingdom of Italy. It currently serves as the seat of the Italian government. The Manor of San Pio V and surrounding gardens stayed in the hands of the House of Chigi's descendants until 2016, when the property was acquired by Link Campus University . Thus, not only does Link Campus University offer the opportunity to study in a highly innovative educational environment , it also offers a campus atmosphere steeped in history and beauty. PEC Atti di notifica Accesso alla Banca Dati di Segreteria Online Procedure elettive Sistema di Assicurazione della Qualità Il sistema AVA (Autovalutazione, Valutazione periodica, Accreditamento) costituisce l’insieme delle attività dell’ANVUR attuative delle disposizioni della legge 20/12/2010, n. 240 e del decreto legislativo 27/01/2012, n. 19. Esso ha l’obiettivo di migliorare la qualità della didattica, della ricerca, della terza missione/impatto sociale e delle altre attività istituzionali e gestionali svolte negli Atenei, attraverso l’applicazione di un modello di Assicurazione della Qualità (AQ) fondato su procedure interne di progettazione, gestione, autovalutazione e miglioramento delle attività formative e scientifiche e su una verifica esterna effettuata in modo chiaro e trasparente. L’Ateneo, in ottemperanza ai requisiti previsti dal sistema AVA e in applicazione delle politiche della qualità adottate dal Senato Accademico e dal Consiglio di Amministrazione, si è dotata di un modello per l’assicurazione e il miglioramento della qualità dei propri servizi e delle proprie attività di Didattica, Ricerca e Terza Missione/Impatto Sociale nell’interesse di studenti, docenti, personale di supporto, ex allievi, rappresentanti del mondo del lavoro. Esso ha l’obiettivo di migliorare la qualità della didattica, della ricerca, della terza missione/impatto sociale e delle altre attività istituzionali e gestionali svolte negli Atenei, attraverso l’applicazione di un modello di Assicurazione della Qualità (AQ) fondato su procedure interne di progettazione, gestione, autovalutazione e miglioramento delle attività formative e scientifiche e su una verifica esterna effettuata in modo chiaro e trasparente. L’Ateneo, in ottemperanza ai requisiti previsti dal sistema AVA e in applicazione delle politiche della qualità adottate dal Senato Accademico e dal Consiglio di Amministrazione, si è dotata di un modello per l’assicurazione e il miglioramento della qualità dei propri servizi e delle proprie attività di Didattica, Ricerca e Terza Missione/Impatto Sociale nell’interesse di studenti, docenti, personale di supporto, ex allievi, rappresentanti del mondo del lavoro. PEC Atti di notifica Accesso alla Banca Dati di Segreteria Online Procedure elettive Sistema di Assicurazione della Qualità Il sistema AVA (Autovalutazione, Valutazione periodica, Accreditamento) costituisce l’insieme delle attività dell’ANVUR attuative delle disposizioni della legge 20/12/2010, n. 240 e del decreto legislativo 27/01/2012, n. 19. Esso ha l’obiettivo di migliorare la qualità della didattica, della ricerca, della terza missione/impatto sociale e delle altre attività istituzionali e gestionali svolte negli Atenei, attraverso l’applicazione di un modello di Assicurazione della Qualità (AQ) fondato su procedure interne di progettazione, gestione, autovalutazione e miglioramento delle attività formative e scientifiche e su una verifica esterna effettuata in modo chiaro e trasparente. L’Ateneo, in ottemperanza ai requisiti previsti dal sistema AVA e in applicazione delle politiche della qualità adottate dal Senato Accademico e dal Consiglio di Amministrazione, si è dotata di un modello per l’assicurazione e il miglioramento della qualità dei propri servizi e delle proprie attività di Didattica, Ricerca e Terza Missione/Impatto Sociale nell’interesse di studenti, docenti, personale di supporto, ex allievi, rappresentanti del mondo del lavoro.
